skill.name: find-bugs
skill.description: Review current-branch changes for bugs, security vulnerabilities, and meaningful code quality issues using complete diff analysis and evidence-based verification.
skill.summary: Audit branch changes for verified bugs and security risks without modifying code.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline-code formatting around a fixed Git diff command. The command is read-only and contains no user-controlled interpolation. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Get the FULL diff: `git diff master...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 12 contains a fixed Git command inside Markdown inline-code delimiters, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The command reads a branch diff and includes no user-controlled interpolation or write operation.

content.user_title: Find Bugs and Security Risks in Branch Changes
content.value_statement: Incomplete code reviews can miss exploitable flaws and behavior regressions. This skill examines the full branch diff, verifies each issue, and reports prioritized fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reads the complete difference between master and the current branch.
Maps changed code to inputs, database queries, authorization checks, state operations, external calls, and cryptography.
Checks each changed file against defined security, reliability, and business logic risks.
Verifies potential issues against surrounding code and existing tests before reporting them.
Produces prioritized findings with locations, severity, evidence, fixes, and relevant standards.
Reports unverified areas and avoids inventing findings when no significant issue exists.
limitations: Assumes master is the comparison branch and may need adjustment for repositories with another base branch.
Reviews only visible local branch changes and their accessible context.
Does not modify code or apply fixes.
Cannot prove runtime behavior when tests, dependencies, or environment details are unavailable.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Inspect proposed changes for regressions, security flaws, and missing tests before opening a pull request.
use_cases.target_user: Software developers preparing a pull request

use_cases.title: Audit Sensitive Changes
use_cases.description: Examine authentication, authorization, sessions, external calls, and data handling for exploitable weaknesses.

use_cases.title: Assess a Release Candidate
use_cases.description: Identify significant branch risks, verify evidence, and prioritize fixes before a release decision.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Branch Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current branch against master. Find significant bugs and security vulnerabilities, verify each finding, and skip style-only comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused first review of a small feature branch.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the current branch for injection, access control, session, cryptography, disclosure, denial-of-service, and business logic risks. Provide evidence and fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when changed code processes untrusted input or sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Authorization and State Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review every changed authorization and state transition. Check ownership, role boundaries, race conditions, invalid transitions, and test coverage before reporting findings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for workflows involving accounts, permissions, or shared resources.

prompt_templates.title: Comprehensive Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Read every changed file completely, map the attack surface, apply the full checklist, verify each issue in context, and disclose unresolved review gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a high-assurance review before release approval.

output_examples.input: Review this branch for significant bugs and security vulnerabilities.
output: High severity: An order update verifies login but does not verify resource ownership.
Evidence: The caller can provide another account's order identifier, and no later ownership check exists.
Fix: Scope the lookup to the authenticated account and add a cross-account access test.

output_examples.input: Audit the changes for race conditions and business logic errors.
output: Medium severity: Two concurrent requests can consume the same remaining quota.
Evidence: The quota is checked before a separate update, without an atomic condition.
Fix: Use one conditional update and test simultaneous requests.

output_examples.input: Report only verified issues and disclose any review gaps.
output_examples.output: No significant verified issues were found. Runtime behavior remains unverified because the required integration environment was unavailable.

best_practices: Provide the intended base branch when it is not master.
Make all changed files and relevant tests available for complete verification.
Share expected behavior for business rules that code alone cannot establish.
anti_patterns: Do not request style-only feedback when the goal is risk discovery.
Do not treat an unverified suspicion as a confirmed vulnerability.
Do not use the review as a substitute for tests or runtime security controls.

faq.question: What changes does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews differences between master and the current branch, then reads changed files when more context is required.

faq.question: Does it modify source code?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and concrete fixes, leaving implementation decisions to the user.

faq.question: What issues receive the highest priority?
faq.answer: Security vulnerabilities receive priority, followed by functional bugs and meaningful code quality problems.

faq.question: How does it reduce false positives?
faq.answer: It checks surrounding code, existing protections, and relevant tests before presenting an issue as real.

faq.question: Does it report formatting concerns?
faq.answer: No. The review excludes stylistic and formatting issues.

faq.question: What happens when verification is incomplete?
faq.answer: The report identifies unverified areas and explains why they could not be confirmed.
